title: Affine norm for a two-point law
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, and let $x,y,\lambda\in\mathbb R$ with $x\ne y$ and $0\le\lambda\le1$. Suppose $\mu(X=x)=\lambda$ and $\mu(X=y)=1-\lambda$. For $q>0$ and $a,b\in\mathbb R$, $N_q(a+bX)^2=\left(\lambda|a+bx|^q+(1-\lambda)|a+by|^q\right)^{2/q}$.
replaced: Let $X$ be measurable on a probability space, let $x\ne y$ and $0\le\lambda\le1$, and suppose $\Pr[X=x]=\lambda$ and $\Pr[X=y]=1-\lambda$. For $q>0$ and $a,b\in\bbr$, $\|a+bX\|_q^2=(\lambda|a+bx|^q+(1-\lambda)|a+by|^q)^{2/q}$.
